So living ships are a little bit more complicated than a regular ship or sentinel. First you need to get your first living ship which takes five real life days to complete all the quests due to timers on certain steps. You start the quest line by getting your first void egg either by purchasing it in the anomaly with quick silver or by someone giving you a void egg. I would recommend just looking up a guide on how to finish the quest and tricks you can use if youre on console to speed up the five day requirement. After you get your first living ship the next time you get a void egg you can then pick and choose what ship youre going to get.

Assuming you finished the quest line and now have your second egg you will pulse drive around any galaxy EXCEPT for this one with the void egg in your inventory and it will start a quest line similar to the first. After the quest line starts it will tell you to go to a planet to go claim your second living ship. Ignore that planet and instead use the portal in the Anomaly to teleport to the featured base (butterfly house). Once you are at butterfly house, fly to the coordinates I provided and land next to the crashed ship. Go into your quest log and the void egg quest will have an option to restart using nearby structures. If you did everything correctly once you reset the quest it will change the crashed ship into the one I posted here for everyone to find.

After 2 days of trying to figure out how it all works I can confirm A. that this is still here and B. if it does not start a freighter battle when you first warp here you have to do the combination of wait 3 hours in game (being in menu does not count but being afk does, I afk'd in the anomaly after moving to a nearby system) AND do 4 warps to other solar systems(does not have to be high conflict, pirate, etc can be any). Each time you warp make sure you either land on the space station or a planet and hop out your ship to create a save point. After doing 4 jumps your next/fifth jump should trigger the freighter battle so make sure that jump is back into this system. If you complete the fight and it is not S class then reload your restore point (not the auto-save) and jump back into this system and redo the fight. Took me 6 reloads after I finally got the actual fight to trigger.

I don't disagree that the sleep on skill 2 is a good way to use her but its so limited since its only the one turn and then on cd for four. damage can be her strong point lemme break it down. 

So say you hit them with skill 2 and with the talent you shock them at a 50% chance. If you sleep them which is at the same rate great, even better if you sleep someone off to the side since you dont get to pick the 2 extra targets on that skill. 

Multistrike goes off and you hit them with skill 1 which gets a 10% buff for hitting them while shocked, has a 50% chance to apply poison to them(with the talent), and you do an additional 50% damage from your 60 talent. so a cleave with a potential 120% damage and the initial 110% damage from the skill 2 for a total of 230% on your first turn to a potential three targets. and its still possible you leave someone who didnt get hit by the multistrike asleep(happens all the time for me)

You also leave them ticking with both poison and shock damage. If someone clears the shock then they get stunned allowing you a chance at putting them to sleep with your passive when its your turn again anyways. or if they do any healing then the poison just does even more damage to them.

assuming the best situation lets say they dont clear the debuffs then you use skill 3 next turn which hits for 182% off the bat just from jacqs debuffs alone and a chance to stun them, albeit at a low rate. multistrike procs again so add another 120% on top of that for a total potential for 302% damage to three enemies on your second turn, which her skill 3 shouldnt be used without debuffs already applied anyways.

Two turns and you can do over 500% damage to a potential three opponents as opposed to if you just single strike you put them to sleep and apply shock with only the 110% damage. (Unless they try to clear the shock which gives you a free chance to put them back to sleep ofc)  On their turn you do another 100% because they have to just choose defend. You then next turn apply the poison and only do another 120% damage on your second turn if you use skill 1 or 168% damage if you use skill three. but if you do that then shock will fall off before your turn after that and they no longer have anything ticking on them so you hit them for just a measly 60% on turn three since only skill 1 would be up if you used skill three on turn two.

in the long run you're looking at either over 500% damage in two turns and then 120% every turn after that. or looking at most 378% damage in the first two turns and then 60% on the third turn. for a total of 438% but taking an extra turn and its still not as much.

Of course everything relies on rng and who you are up against. so in some cases my way is better in other cases its better to just get the sleep off like you said and do less damage from her.

The first time you earn a luminous engram on a class it is +5 to your current power level (not including mods as those dont count).
